blocks.text: Application Inventory provides a centralized inventory of predefined private application types available in your environment. It helps you discover supported application types, understand their classifications, and use consistent application definitions when configuring private applications.

Application Inventory automatically discovers and classifies private application traffic to identify application types without relying on specific ports or protocols. It also works with SSL/TLS-encrypted traffic without requiring traffic decryption, enabling consistent application identification across your environment.
Application Inventory provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Use standardized application definitions to simplify and maintain consistent private application configurations.
Gain deeper visibility into private application traffic to better understand your application environment.
Improve application security by enabling more accurate application identification and supporting consistent least-privilege access policies.
Automatically discover and classify private applications.

blocks.text: During the current implementation phase, the inventory displays only predefined application types. Support for creating and managing custom application types will be introduced in a future release.
On the Application Inventory page (Private Access > Private Applications > Application Inventory), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Show or hide filters to filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. To learn more, see Using Tables.

Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see Using Tables.
View the predefined application types across all supported categories. For each application type, you can see:
App Type: The predefined application type that determines the type of private application that can be configured.
Before you configure a new private application, you can use the App Type filter to check if an application type already exists instead of defining a custom type.
Category: The category associated with each application type. Categories make it easier to organize and locate related application types.
Definition: The application type that was created.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
